findings.title: Custody becomes present, witnessed responsibility
findings.claim: At the Book's custody point, inward retention, protection of a binding trust, and present witness join to make authority an answerable public responsibility.
findings.mechanism: The custody form at 5:44:17 carries memory and guarded commitment, while the witness form at 5:44:23 supplies present public presence; guarded-record and testimony connections outside the focus return these forms to a wider pattern of accountable custody.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the custodians as actively holding and publicly bearing the Book, with responsibility continuing in the present.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that rabbis and learned authorities judge by the Torah and witness to it; this finding adds the manner in which their entrusted duty is held and made visible.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and their trusted cross-run finding are exact; the wider connection targets supply Arabic and relation notes but no target morphology, so the cross-surah extension remains bounded.

findings.title: Exchange turns signs into a negotiable equivalent
findings.claim: The exchange verb lets the signs be heard as converted into a negotiable equivalent, with fear of people supplying the pressure to accept the trade.
findings.mechanism: The focus Form VIII exchange verb carries a real transaction, while the neighboring price and smallness words and supplied connections pairing covenant or revealed content with small-price exchange give that transaction a wider valuation frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the small price as the received return in a pressured exchange, so the warning reaches the act of making revelation commensurable with a worldly benefit.
findings.containment: The ordinary prohibition against selling God's signs for a small price remains the ground; the added reading describes the pressure and valuation inside that prohibition without making the image a literal market account.

epistemic.reason: The focus exchange carrier and price terms are exact, and the connection targets supply direct Arabic parallels; the originating reader walk is legacy-unbound and target morphology is absent.

findings.title: Written custody carries the memory of harm forward
findings.claim: The Book's custody can carry the memory of catastrophic harm forward so judgment restrains its recurrence and protects life.
findings.mechanism: The focus judgment form supplies the restraining carrier; the HFT trace attributes to 5:32 a written determination born from murder, disorder, and the preservation of life, and returns that sequence through the two focus judgment occurrences.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader perceives custody as preventive transmission: what is preserved can interrupt repeated harm, not only remain available as a text for later cases.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim about judging by the Torah and witnessing over the Book remains intact; the preventative-memory function is an attributed contextual inference from 5:32, not a complete legal history or a general theory of judgment.

epistemic.reason: The HFT supplies exact Arabic anchors, word indices, roots, roles, and changed reading, but its context segmentation and unresolved branch identities remain attributed rather than independently lexicon-established.

findings.title: No finite price can ransom the liability
findings.claim: The small price can be heard as any finite worldly return accepted for exchanging away a sign, within a liability that no worldly total can ransom.
findings.mechanism: The focus exchange, price, and smallness forms supply the carrier circuit; the HFT trace connects them to 5:36, where everything on earth and its equal are offered as ransom and refused, returning the scale to the focus price.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the received price is small in relation, not merely in amount: even the imagined maximum worldly total cannot purchase release.
findings.containment: The ordinary warning about a small price remains the primary reading; the ransom scene supplies a bounded scale for its devaluation and does not claim that every worldly exchange is the same judgment.

epistemic.reason: The focus carriers and exact HFT context coordinates are supplied, while the ransom and acceptance branches remain unresolved in the independent lexicon and are therefore retained as attributed roles.

findings.containment: The focus still speaks of judging by what God sent down and names the failure to do so; the sanction-repair sequence is an attributed contextual model, not a claim that the ayah prescribes one complete human procedure.

epistemic.reason: The HFT supplies exact Arabic anchors and a changed reading, but its contextual branch identities remain attributed and the sequence is explicitly qualified as an inference.

findings.title: The witness can be inverted into concealment
findings.claim: By analogy, the concluding coverer can become a burial mechanism that places an exposed wrong and its governing witness out of public sight.
findings.mechanism: The focus witness form at 5:44:23 supplies public exposure and the covering predicate at 5:44:41 supplies the inversion; the HFT trace connects those forms to the material concealment of the exposed wrong in 5:31.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees concealment as an active placement of what should remain visible under witness, not only as a failure to repeat a rule.
findings.containment: The ordinary verdict remains that those who fail to judge by what God sent down bear the stated designation; this exploratory analogy does not identify every failed judge with the earlier killer or replace the confessional force of the predicate.

epistemic.reason: The HFT supplies exact focus and context coordinates and an explicit containment note, but two context branches have no independent registry descriptors and the resulting image is marked exploratory.
